title: Worktrees — three features at once
intro: Git worktrees turn one Claude into a team: isolated directories, shared history, parallel sessions.

steps.title: What a worktree is
steps.body: Git worktrees check out **multiple branches of the same repository into separate directories** — each a full working copy with isolated files, all sharing one git history. No clones, no divergent remotes.

steps.title: The workflow
steps.body:
1. **Commit any pending changes** — parallelism starts from a clean tree.
2. `mkdir .trees`
3. Per feature: `git worktree add .trees/ui_feature` (and `testing_feature`, `quality_feature`).
4. Open a terminal **in each worktree**, launch Claude Code in each, assign each its feature.
5. Commit in each worktree; close the sessions.
6. Back in the main terminal: *"use the git merge command to merge in all the worktrees of the .trees folder into main and fix any conflicts if there are any."*

steps.title: The three features
steps.body: The course runs a **UI feature** (dark/light theme toggle), a **testing feature**, and a **code-quality feature** simultaneously — three Claude sessions, three directories, one repo.

points.label: Isolation
points.note: Each session edits its own directory — no stepping on each other's files mid-flight.

points.label: Shared history
points.note: All worktrees are branches of one repo — merging is ordinary git, not repo surgery.

points.label: Throughput
points.note: Independent features land in parallel wall-clock time; the merge is the only serial step.

points.label: Claude merges
points.note: Even conflict resolution is delegated — the final prompt asks Claude to merge all trees and fix conflicts.

steps.title: When not to
steps.body: > [!warn] Worktrees buy throughput only when features are **independent**. Two features touching the same files just move the conflict from your editor to the merge — and a dirty starting tree merges chaos. Commit clean, split independent, merge deliberately.

recap:
**Clean tree → .trees/ per feature → a Claude in each → commit each → Claude merges.**

- Worktrees: isolated directories, one shared history.
- Three independent features land in parallel.
- The merge is the serial step — delegate it, but review it.
- Dependent features don't parallelize; they queue.
